questions.prompt: Why does changing the impersonated user's password fail to invalidate a Golden Ticket?
options: Because password changes take 30 days to replicate
Because the ticket is signed with the krbtgt key and isn't tied to that user's credential at all
Because Golden Tickets automatically re-sign themselves
questions.explanation: A Golden Ticket is forged using the krbtgt hash and asserts an identity rather than proving one. The impersonated account's password is never involved, so changing it has no effect.

questions.prompt: What makes a Silver Ticket stealthier than a Golden Ticket, despite being narrower in scope?
options: It uses stronger encryption that cannot be logged
It is presented directly to the target service and never contacts a domain controller, so DC-side authentication logging never records it
It automatically deletes relevant event logs
It only works outside business hours
questions.explanation: Because a Silver Ticket forges the service ticket itself using a service account's hash, the attacker skips the DC entirely -- removing the DC's opportunity to log the authentication at all.

questions.prompt: Why is a 4769 (service ticket requested) with no preceding 4768 (TGT requested) suspicious?
options: It indicates the domain controller is misconfigured
It suggests the TGT being used was never actually issued by the DC -- consistent with a forged ticket
It means the user's password expired
It is completely normal and expected behavior
questions.explanation: Normally a client obtains a TGT (4768) before requesting service tickets (4769). A service ticket request with no corresponding TGT issuance suggests the TGT was forged rather than granted.

questions.prompt: Why is an arbitrary ticket lifetime possible with a Golden Ticket?
options: Domain policy is applied only to interactive logons
The DC trusts the forged ticket's contents rather than enforcing domain Kerberos lifetime policy against it -- default tooling often issues 10-year tickets
Kerberos has no concept of ticket lifetime
The attacker must still honor the 10-hour domain default
questions.explanation: Because the ticket decrypts correctly with the krbtgt key, the DC accepts its asserted contents -- including a lifetime far beyond what domain policy would ever issue.
